The correct IUPAC name is determined by assigning the principal functional group (carboxylic acid) to position 1, then placing the remaining substituents according to the given relationships: carboxylic acid, carbaldehyde, and cyano are all meta (1,3,5-positions); hydroxyl and dimethylamino are ortho to the acid (2,6-positions); methoxy is para to the acid (4-position). The methoxy and hydroxyl must both be ortho to the cyano, fixing the cyano at position 3 (or 5 in the alternative orientation). Numbering is chosen to give the lowest locant to the alphabetically first substituent (cyano). Alphabetical order is cyano, dimethylamino, formyl, hydroxy, methoxy. This yields the name 3-cyano-6-(dimethylamino)-5-formyl-2-hydroxy-4-methoxybenzoic acid.
